findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar, so other hosts' invites fail
findings.body: For COLLECTIVE events event.destinationCalendar now holds one calendar per host, but this code always takes the first entry (line 73) and never checks which credential is running. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards credential.id, and EventManager passes destination.externalId, but that externalId is only echoed back in the result and never reaches the service. For a team member's Office365 account the URL becomes /me/calendars/<organizer's calendar id>/events, which does not exist in that account, so the member never gets the event. The same pattern exists in Lark createEvent (calendarId taken from destinationCalendar[0], around lines 128-129 of the Lark service) and in CalDAV createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts filters calendars by the first destination's externalId; for a member's account nothing matches, no object is created, and the call still returns success). Only the Google service selects by credentialId, so the collective fix works for Google only.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent falls back to 'primary' instead of the event's calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, the expression searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that falsy value. It never matches, so calendarId becomes undefined and the code falls back to 'primary'. The previous code used event.destinationCalendar?.externalId here. On cancel, the delete goes to the user's primary calendar instead of the calendar holding the event. Google returns 404 and deleteEvent resolves silently, so the event stays on the real calendar with no error. This is reachable for references without externalCalendarId, including those the new EventManager code creates without it.

findings.title: Google updateEvent passes undefined calendarId when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: Same mistake as deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is null, find() compares cal.externalId against null, never matches, and selectedCalendar becomes undefined. The previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Now calendar.events.update is called with calendarId undefined, so updates fail for every reference without externalCalendarId. The new EventManager paths produce exactly such references (see the updateLocation and create findings).

findings.title: Google Meet description patch uses selectedCalendar, which can now be undefined
findings.body: The insert uses 'selectedCalendar || "primary"', but the patch call below uses the raw selectedCalendar. When no destination matches the credential, the patch gets calendarId undefined. The patch is not awaited and has no error handling, so the hangout link description update silently fails for events inserted into primary. The same resolved calendarId should be used in both calls.

findings.title: Google createEvent ignores destinations stored without a credentialId
findings.body: The lookup matches destinations only by cal.credentialId === credentialId. Legacy DestinationCalendar rows with credentialId null never match, so the event goes to 'primary' instead of the configured externalId. The previous code used calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId directly. EventManager's no-credentialId branch (createEvent(c, event) with no destination) makes this path reachable, so users with legacy destination rows get their bookings created in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Unguarded destructured element can throw when no destination calendar exists
findings.body: mainHostDestinationCalendar comes from array destructuring, so its static type is DestinationCalendar, not DestinationCalendar | undefined. When evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty and the location is Google Meet, this line dereferences undefined and throws a TypeError inside create(). The previous code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration, which was safe. Booking creation fails for these events. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

findings.title: externalCalendarId is dropped for destinations created without a destination id
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId in the no-credentialId branch, the fallback branch, and for other_calendar integrations. CalendarManager.createEvent then returns externalId undefined, so result.externalId is undefined and the booking reference is saved without externalCalendarId. The previous code persisted evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Later update and delete calls then have no calendar id to work with (see the Google updateEvent and deleteEvent findings).

findings.title: updateLocation writes calendar references with no credentialId or externalCalendarId
findings.body: CalendarManager.updateEvent returns only appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError and calWarnings. It never returns externalId or credentialId, so result.externalId and result.credentialId are always undefined here. editLocation.handler persists these via references.create, so the new calendar reference rows lack credentialId and externalCalendarId. The previous code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId and externalId. A later cancel then takes the legacy no-credentialId path in handleCancelBooking, which deletes using all calendar credentials of that type and no calendar id.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes shape and empty value is inconsistent
findings.body: evt is spread into webhook payloads (sendPayload with ...evt), so destinationCalendar in BOOKING_CANCELLED and other webhooks changes from a DestinationCalendar object or null to an array. This is an undocumented breaking change for webhook consumers. Empty is now [] here but null in handleNewBooking (BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED), so consumers checking for null get different values per event type. The e2e expectation change from null to [] in webhook.e2e.ts (line 249) confirms the public payload changed.

findings.title: Cancel loop repeats recurring and legacy deletions once per calendar reference
findings.body: The former single if was turned into a loop over all calendar references, but the recurring branch does not depend on the reference. For a recurring series cancelled with allRemainingBookings, it deletes every updated booking's events across all user calendar credentials once per reference, so a collective series with N references issues N times the deletes and pushes duplicate entries into apiDeletes. The legacy no-credentialId branch likewise re-runs for each reference lacking credentialId. The loop should be restructured so the recurring deletion runs once.

findings.title: Team members' calendars are silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. Then evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) is a no-op, so for a COLLECTIVE event the team members' destination calendars are never added. EventManager sees no destinations and falls back to a single calendar for the organizer, so the other hosts never get the event. Initialise the array before pushing, or build the combined list in one place.

findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The original code was '...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })', so slug was set when billing was disabled. The new '...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})' sets slug only when billing is enabled. Self-hosted instances (billing disabled) will now create organizations without a slug. Billing-enabled instances will get the slug immediately, bypassing the requested-slug flow. This change is unrelated to the PR's collective-host fix and is not explained in the description.

findings.title: Calendar update failures are no longer logged
findings.body: The console.error(message) in the catch block was removed, but the message is still built with the error details. Failures in updateAllCalendarEvents now return error result objects without any log entry, so the cause of a failed calendar update is lost.

findings.title: organization.slug removed from dynamic-group user select without explanation
findings.body: The findMany for dynamic group users dropped 'organization: { select: { slug: true } }'. The PR description does not mention it. If any code later in handleNewBooking reads organization.slug for dynamic-group bookings, it now gets undefined. Confirm there are no remaining readers or restore the select.

findings.title: loadUsers catch-all turns client errors into a generic 500
findings.body: Any error that is not an HttpError or PrismaClientKnownRequestError, including the new plain Error for an empty dynamicUserList (which is a client input problem), is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users'. The original message is discarded, and a request validation problem looks like a server fault. Prisma known errors are mapped to 400, which is also a questionable classification for database failures.

findings.title: Multi-destination calendar creation has no tests
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents now loops over several destinations, fetches credentials from the DB for other hosts, and handles the no-credentialId path differently. updateAllCalendarEvents also loops over multiple references. The only test-file change is one e2e expectation. Several regressions listed above (missing externalCalendarId, dropped credentialId, wrong calendar selection) would be caught by unit tests that run EventManager with a two-destination collective event against mocked calendar services.
